{
  "method": "Financial managers make three main types of decisions: investment, financing, and dividend decisions. The investment decision involves calculating the cost of capital using the weighted average cost of capital (WACC) formula, which is (cost of debt * debt weight + cost of equity * equity weight) / total weight. The financing decision involves calculating the cost of debt and equity, and the dividend decision involves calculating the dividend payout ratio.",
   "calculations": [
       {"label": "WACC", "expression": "(0.06 * 0.4 + 0.12 * 0.6) / 1"},
       {"label": "cost of debt", "expression": "0.08 / (1 - 0.25)"},
       {"label": "cost of equity", "expression": "0.10 + 0.05 * (1.2 - 0.05)"},
       {"label": "dividend payout ratio", "expression": "0.5 / (1 + 0.1)"}
   ],
   "keyPoints": [
       "identification of investment decisions",
       "identification of financing decisions",
       "identification of dividend decisions",
       "calculation of weighted average cost of capital (WACC)",
       "calculation of cost of debt",
       "calculation of cost of equity",
       "calculation of dividend payout ratio"
   ]
}

The investment decision involves calculating the cost of capital using the weighted average cost of capital (WACC) formula, which is (cost of debt * debt weight + cost of equity * equity weight) / total weight. The financing decision involves calculating the cost of debt and equity, and the dividend decision involves calculating the dividend payout ratio.
keyPoints: calculation of weighted average cost of capital (WACC)
